## 1. `prompt_cache_key` (decision D8)

**What changed.**

- **Where the key comes from.** `AgentRequest` gained `chat_key`. `AgentHost::make_agent_request` sets it to `<projectId>/<conversationId>`, for example `p-3f…9a-1c…77/c-2`. That is one added line in `AgentHost.cpp`, next to `request_id`.
- **How it reaches the codec.** `ProviderAgent::begin_transcript` copies it to `TurnTranscript::chat_key`.
- **What the codec sends.** `ResponsesCodec::build` sends it as `prompt_cache_key` on reply requests.

**Why a new field was needed.** The chat id was not available at the codec before. `request_id` contains the project and chat ids, but also the message id and attempt, so it changes on every turn.

**When no key is sent:**

- **Title requests.** They have no `chat_key`.
- **The account provider (JusPrin Cloud, `account_sign_in`).** See the gateway section.
- **Length.** A project id is at most 35 characters (`"p-"` plus two 64-bit hex numbers, `default_uuid()` in `ProjectPersistence.cpp`), so keys are about 40 characters. OpenAI's limit is undocumented. One community report says 64 characters; **unverified**.

**Tests.**

- `test_agent_bridge.cpp`, "every request of a chat carries one prompt_cache_key, and another chat another". It runs on the real host and loop. Chat A has a person turn with a slice call (two requests) and the app's turn after the slice. Chat B has one request. All three of chat A's requests carry `projectId/c-1`, and chat B's carries `projectId/c-2`.
- `test_openai_responses_agent.cpp`, "a request carries its chat's prompt_cache_key, except through JusPrin's gateway and for a title". It is a codec-level test covering:
  - OpenAI and OpenRouter get the key
  - the gateway does not
  - a title request does not
  - an empty key sends nothing

The `[history-prefix]` guard compares every non-prompt body field across requests. It stays unchanged, which confirms that the key does not vary within a chat.

**OpenRouter.** Its Responses API reference lists `prompt_cache_key` as an accepted optional string, but does not say what it does. Whether OpenRouter forwards it to OpenAI is **unverified**.

### Gateway finding (verified by reading the source)

The gateway source is on this machine: `/Users/kenneth/Projects/tsd-enterprise`, branch `master` at `7ab63cc151`, the same as `origin/master`. See `web_ent/jusprin/v2/upstream.py`.

- **Unknown fields are refused, not forwarded.** `ALLOWED_FIELDS['responses']` is `model, store, stream, parallel_tool_calls, instructions, tools, input, reasoning`. `prepare()` answers any other top-level field with `400 invalid_request "Field "prompt_cache_key" is not allowed."`. Sending the key through the gateway would have failed every OpenAI-format JusPrin Cloud request. That is why the codec skips it for `account_sign_in`.
- **The gateway is where the key matters most.** Every JusPrin Cloud user shares one OpenAI organisation, and the gateway prepends the same identity line to `instructions`. So all cloud chats open identically and land on the same cache machines.
  - **Follow-up:** add `prompt_cache_key` to `ALLOWED_FIELDS['responses']` in tsd-enterprise and deploy it. Then drop `&& !profile.account_sign_in` in `ResponsesCodec::build`.
  - **Order matters:** the app change must not ship before the gateway one.
  - Whether the deployed gateway matches `master` is **unverified**. The plan says it went live 2026-10-25 as obi.4048.
- **Anthropic format.** `messages` are forwarded as sent, `cache_control` included, and the gateway's identity text goes in a block of its own before the client's `system` block. Only `metadata` is dropped.
- **For R2/R6.**
  - In-array `role: "system"` messages and `developer` items pass through untouched, because the gateway does not inspect `messages` or `input`.
  - The gateway sends upstream only its backend's configured headers (`_headers()` in `upstream.py`), never the client's.
  - So R2's `clear_at` beta header (`anthropic-beta: mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21`) reaches Anthropic only if it is added to the alias backend's `headers` in `JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES`. Without it, `clear_at` is rejected as an unknown field.

## 2. A stable tool list

**Before.**

- `offered_tools` in `ProviderAgent.cpp` offered `object_import` only when the request's message had an importable model attachment. The turn that attached a model therefore sent a different tool list from the turn before and the turn after. On Anthropic that means a cold cache for the whole chat, twice.
- A call to `object_import` on any other turn was refused as `unknown_tool` before it ran.
- A call whose attachment could not be resolved failed with `not_found`: "The attached model is no longer available".

**Now.**

- **Registry.** `object_import` has `ToolAvailability::Always`. `ImportableAttachment` is removed from the enum.
- **Execution.** In `ToolExecutionCoordinator::execute`, an `attachmentId` that resolves to no stored model file fails with `invalid_arguments`, with the message: `No model file attached in this chat has the id "<id>". Nothing was imported. Use an attachment id from the person's message; if they attached no model file, ask them to attach it.`
- **Why `invalid_arguments`.**
  - It keeps the call in the "fix the call" group of `ToolErrors.hpp`, where `unknown_tool` already put it.
  - `not_found` means "read the state again, then call again", and re-reading the workspace cannot find an attachment.
  - The "Ask the person" codes (`opened_before`, `workspace_unavailable`) mean other conditions.
  - The message names the step.
- **Side effect.** A model attached in an earlier message of the chat can now be imported later, because the resolver looks the id up in the whole document.

**Tests.**

- `test_agent_bridge.cpp`, "the tool list is the same on every request of a chat, whatever a message attaches". It runs on the real host with the Anthropic wire format:
  - turn 1 has no attachment
  - turn 2 attaches a model and imports it, adding one object
  - turn 3 calls `object_import` with an id that names nothing
  - all 5 requests carry byte-identical `tools`, `object_import` included
  - the turn-3 call comes back as an `is_error` result with `invalid_arguments` and the message, and adds no object

It failed 5 of 28 assertions: the attachment turn's two requests carried a different tool list, and the turn-3 call got `unknown_tool`. I then restored the source.
- `test_tool_coordinator.cpp`: the unresolvable-attachment case now expects `invalid_arguments` and the exact message.
- `test_openai_responses_agent.cpp`: the tool list with a model attachment equals the list without one.

## 3. The Anthropic cache breakpoint and skill text

**Where the breakpoints are today** (`AnthropicCodec.cpp`, all `{"type":"ephemeral"}`):

1. The last tool (`tools_json`, line 87).
2. The single `system` block (`build`, line 272).
3. The last block of the newest `user` message after role normalisation (`build`, line 262). It moves forward on every request.

A fired skill is sent as an in-array `role: "system"` message right after the user content or the tool results that fired it (`push_skills`). Its picture is a user image block, which merges into that user message, so the picture sits before breakpoint 3 and is cached. The skill text sits after it.

- On the request that fires it, the skill text is billed uncached at 1x.
- On the next request of the turn it is written to the cache at 1.25x.

That is M1's leak.

**Bytes after the last breakpoint, 26 recorded bodies.**

- **Method.** Each body was mapped to the Anthropic codec's message layout: developer items become system messages, then the codec's merge and normalisation rules apply. Then I counted the compact JSON after the breakpoint block.
- **Script.** `/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin--claude-worktrees-cache-r8-f275c7/c449884d-06ef-4be3-ae77-8382bf117ba4/scratchpad/r8/after_breakpoint.py`, run as `python3 -I <script> tests/project_prompt/requests.json`.
- **Scope.** The system prompt and tools, about 41 KB, come before breakpoints 1 and 2 and are not counted.

| case | after the last breakpoint today (bytes) | of which skill text |
|---|---|---|
| model-imported-by-tool, model-opened-by-tool, model-opened-unnamed | 8,520 each | 8,446 (file-loaded) |
| advice-infill, answer-from-context, direct-change, issue-explain, issue-fix, loaded-vs-configured, reply-in-german, slice-warnings-ready, troubleshoot-first-layer | 5,309 each | 5,210 (print issues) |
| slice-refused-by-tool, slice-refused-then-ready | 3,640 each | 3,577 (slice failed) |
| after-intent | 1,329 | 1,288 (setup changed) |
| the other 11 cases | 0 | 0 |

- 15 of 26 bodies have bytes after the breakpoint, totalling 81,950. In every case it is one trailing system message holding the skill.
- With a breakpoint on the skill it would be 0 in every case.

**Why I did not move the breakpoint.** Source: Anthropic's mid-conversation system messages page (`platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-system-messages`), read 2026-10-29.

- **Under R2 it is an error.** R2 sends skills as turn-scoped messages (`clear_at: "next_user_message"`). The page says such a message carries "no `cache_control`" ("A cleared message is never part of a cache key, so a breakpoint on it could never match"). The API answers `cache_control is not permitted on a turn-scoped system message` with a 400. It says to "Put the breakpoint on the last block of the preceding user turn instead". Its agent-loop example puts it on the last `tool_result`. That is exactly today's breakpoint 3.
- **Today it is undocumented.** For a plain (`clear_at: "never"`) system message, the page says it "is itself cacheable", and that on the next turn "you can move your cache breakpoint past it". It never says `cache_control` is allowed on its blocks. Verifying that would need a live call, so I made none.

The rule was to change the placement only if it is right under both today's behaviour and R2's. Moving the breakpoint onto the skill is right under neither for certain, and is a 400 under R2. The code is unchanged.

**Recommendation for R2.**

1. **Keep breakpoint 3 where it is**, on the last block of the newest user message, which is the user turn before any skill. Never put `cache_control` on a turn-scoped message.
2. **The leak goes away under R2 without a breakpoint change.** The page says a turn-scoped message "renders only while no `role: "user"` message comes after it" and "A user message that carries only `tool_result` blocks counts". A cleared message "costs no input tokens".
   - So under R2 a skill's text is billed once, on the request that fires it, and is never written to the cache.
   - Today the same text is billed at 1x, then written at 1.25x, then read on the turn's later requests.
   - The 81,950 bytes above stay after the breakpoint on the firing request, but stop being written to the cache one request late.
3. **The clearing request reads the right entry.** The page says that on the request that clears a message, "the reusable cached prefix ends at the user turn before it, so only the one assistant turn between that message and the new user message is reprocessed". The entry it reads is the one breakpoint 3 wrote on the firing request. That is another reason not to move breakpoint 3.
4. **A design point R2 must settle (behaviour, not cost).** Because a `tool_result` message clears a turn-scoped message, the model sees the skill only on the request that fired it, not "for the rest of the turn".
   - That matches what the Responses codec does today, since it drops the skill from the next request.
   - It does not match today's Anthropic codec, which keeps the skill visible for the rest of the turn.
   - If the plan's "cleared at the next user message" meant the next message from the person, `clear_at` does not do that.
5. **A message after a tool result on smaller models.** The plan already notes that Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 may ignore a system message placed right after a tool result. Under R2 that is the only place a skill fired by a result can go.

**TTL (decision D7).** Confirmed: the codec sends no `ttl`. `ephemeral()` is `{"type":"ephemeral"}` at all three breakpoints, so the 5-minute default applies. Nothing in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/` mentions `ttl` or `1h`. The gateway forwards `cache_control` unchanged.

## Problem

The chat-history cache work has to check that each model request opens with the bytes of the one before it. No full request body was kept anywhere. The prompt-test recorder's `requests.json` holds bodies for its own suite, with stored results cut at 4,000 characters, and the live harness modes printed only token counts.

## What I built

- **`tests/jusprin_support/RequestLog.hpp`** (header-only, so the harness and `agent_bridge_tests` share it with no CMake change). `RequestLog::transport(provider, inner)` wraps any `IAgentHttpTransport`; `RequestLog::agent(inner)` wraps any `IAgentService`, so the log knows each request's purpose (reply or title), request id and attempt. For the n-th request of a run it writes:
  - `NNNN-request.json`: the body exactly as the transport was given it, written before it is forwarded.
  - `NNNN-request.meta.json`: provider, URL, headers (`Authorization`, `x-api-key` and other credential headers redacted; `Idempotency-Key` kept), project id and chat id (chat ids restart in each project), purpose, request id, attempt, post time, body length.
  - `NNNN-response.sse`: the response stream as received.
  - `NNNN-response.json`: outcome (complete, error, cancelled, replaced, not_started), HTTP status, usage with the provider's own field names (Anthropic `cache_read_input_tokens`/`cache_creation_input_tokens` come through as-is), stop reason, assembled text, error. It reads both the Messages and the Responses stream.
- **Shell harness flag `--request-log <dir>`**, for `--live-agent`, `--manual-live-agent` and `--project-prompt-requests`. It refuses a non-empty directory and any other mode (exit 2). Documented in the header comment of `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp` (where all flags are documented; there is no `tests/shell/README.md`) and in a new section of `tests/project_prompt/README.md`.
- **`tests/project_prompt/prefix_check.py LOG_DIR [--ignore-key KEY] [--json]`**. For consecutive requests of the same project, chat and purpose it reports the common byte prefix, the first differing byte, the JSON path of that byte in each body, and the path of the last differing byte. `[append]` means the later body is the earlier one with items added at the end of one array and every other byte unchanged. `--ignore-key cache_control` drops Anthropic's moving breakpoint (then the bodies are compared as Python re-serialises them, and the output says so). Unit tests: `tests/project_prompt/test_prefix_check.py`.

## How I verified it

- **Catch2** `[request-log]` in `tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp` (appended at the end): two turns on the real host and provider loop, once per wire format, against the existing `RecordingProvider` fake. Each logged reply body equals the bytes the fake received; usage, stop reason, text, project and chat id, numbering and redaction are checked. I proved it can fail: making the logger append one byte to each body gave 4 byte-equality failures and 8 length failures; restored, it passes (150 assertions).
- **Whole agent suite**: 471 test cases, 16,575 assertions, all passed (Release build in this worktree).
- **`test_prefix_check.py`**: 9 tests pass. The "an append followed by a later change is not an append" test fails when the tail condition is removed.
- **Scripted harness run**: `--project-prompt-requests` on the `direct` conversation of `script.json` (two passes, scripted model, nothing sent over the network) with `--request-log` wrote 333 requests (1,332 files, largest body 1.4 MB). `prefix_check.py` reported all 329 pairs as `[append]` and took 7 seconds. The recorder's own output file was byte-identical with and without `--request-log`. `requests.json` and the baselines are untouched.

## What I could not verify, and things to know

- **No live run.** No model was called. The Anthropic path is tested only through the Catch2 fake; the Responses path through the fake and the scripted harness run. Real streams (OpenAI's `response.completed` usage, Anthropic's `message_start`/`message_delta` usage) follow the documented shapes the codecs already parse, but no real stream has gone through this logger yet.
- **The live harness mode only builds an OpenAI agent** on this branch. The Anthropic journey mode (`--plan-journey`) is uncommitted in `.claude/worktrees/opus-cost-batch`; to log it, wrap its `make_openai_http_transport()` with `log.transport("anthropic", …)` and its agent with `log.agent(…)`, the same way `install_harness_agent` does.
- **Not logged**: the printer panel's Agent and any agent the host rebuilds through its chat model source (a chat that picks a model other than the one the harness installed). Both are built from the app configuration through `make_openai_http_transport()` in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Covering them needs a small seam in production code (for example a test-settable transport wrapper used by `make_openai_http_transport`); I did not add one.
- **Reading the byte count on OpenAI**: the app writes JSON keys alphabetically, so a Responses body opens with `input` and has `instructions` and `tools` after it. The shared byte count of a clean append is then just the earlier `input`; read the kind and the last-difference path, not the count. This is about the JSON byte order only

- **Where the key comes from.** `AgentRequest` gained `chat_key`. `AgentHost::make_agent_request` sets it to `<projectId>/<conversationId>`, for example `p-3f…9a-1c…77/c-2`. That is one added line in `AgentHost.cpp`, next to `request_id`.
- **How it reaches the codec.** `ProviderAgent::begin_transcript` copies it to `TurnTranscript::chat_key`.
- **What the codec sends.** `ResponsesCodec::build` sends it as `prompt_cache_key` on reply requests.

**Why a new field was needed.** The chat id was not available at the codec before. `request_id` contains the project and chat ids, but also the message id and attempt, so it changes on every turn.

**When no key is sent:**

- **Title requests.** They have no `chat_key`.
- **The account provider (JusPrin Cloud, `account_sign_in`).** See the gateway section.
- **Length.** A project id is at most 35 characters (`"p-"` plus two 64-bit hex numbers, `default_uuid()` in `ProjectPersistence.cpp`), so keys are about 40 characters. OpenAI's limit is undocumented. One community report says 64 characters; **unverified**.

**Tests.**

- `test_agent_bridge.cpp`, "every request of a chat carries one prompt_cache_key, and another chat another". It runs on the real host and loop. Chat A has a person turn with a slice call (two requests) and the app's turn after the slice. Chat B has one request. All three of chat A's requests carry `projectId/c-1`, and chat B's carries `projectId/c-2`.
- `test_openai_responses_agent.cpp`, "a request carries its chat's prompt_cache_key, except through JusPrin's gateway and for a title". It is a codec-level test covering:
  - OpenAI and OpenRouter get the key
  - the gateway does not
  - a title request does not
  - an empty key sends nothing

The `[history-prefix]` guard compares every non-prompt body field across requests. It stays unchanged, which confirms that the key does not vary within a chat.

**OpenRouter.** Its Responses API reference lists `prompt_cache_key` as an accepted optional string, but does not say what it does. Whether OpenRouter forwards it to OpenAI is **unverified**.

### Gateway finding (verified by reading the source)

The gateway source is on this machine: `/Users/kenneth/Projects/tsd-enterprise`, branch `master` at `7ab63cc151`, the same as `origin/master`. See `web_ent/jusprin/v2/upstream.py`.

- **Unknown fields are refused, not forwarded.** `ALLOWED_FIELDS['responses']` is `model, store, stream, parallel_tool_calls, instructions, tools, input, reasoning`. `prepare()` answers any other top-level field with `400 invalid_request "Field "prompt_cache_key" is not allowed."`. Sending the key through the gateway would have failed every OpenAI-format JusPrin Cloud request. That is why the codec skips it for `account_sign_in`.
- **The gateway is where the key matters most.** Every JusPrin Cloud user shares one OpenAI organisation, and the gateway prepends the same identity line to `instructions`. So all cloud chats open identically and land on the same cache machines.
  - **Follow-up:** add `prompt_cache_key` to `ALLOWED_FIELDS['responses']` in tsd-enterprise and deploy it. Then drop `&& !profile.account_sign_in` in `ResponsesCodec::build`.
  - **Order matters:** the app change must not ship before the gateway one.
  - Whether the deployed gateway matches `master` is **unverified**. The plan says it went live 2026-10-25 as obi.4048.
- **Anthropic format.** `messages` are forwarded as sent, `cache_control` included, and the gateway's identity text goes in a block of its own before the client's `system` block. Only `metadata` is dropped.
- **For R2/R6.**
  - In-array `role: "system"` messages and `developer` items pass through untouched, because the gateway does not inspect `messages` or `input`.
  - The gateway sends upstream only its backend's configured headers (`_headers()` in `upstream.py`), never the client's.
  - So R2's `clear_at` beta header (`anthropic-beta: mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21`) reaches Anthropic only if it is added to the alias backend's `headers` in `JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES`. Without it, `clear_at` is rejected as an unknown field.

## 2. A stable tool list

**Before.**

- `offered_tools` in `ProviderAgent.cpp` offered `object_import` only when the request's message had an importable model attachment. The turn that attached a model therefore sent a different tool list from the turn before and the turn after. On Anthropic that means a cold cache for the whole chat, twice.
- A call to `object_import` on any other turn was refused as `unknown_tool` before it ran.
- A call whose attachment could not be resolved failed with `not_found`: "The attached model is no longer available".

**Now.**

- **Registry.** `object_import` has `ToolAvailability::Always`. `ImportableAttachment` is removed from the enum.
- **Execution.** In `ToolExecutionCoordinator::execute`, an `attachmentId` that resolves to no stored model file fails with `invalid_arguments`, with the message: `No model file attached in this chat has the id "<id>". Nothing was imported. Use an attachment id from the person's message; if they attached no model file, ask them to attach it.`
- **Why `invalid_arguments`.**
  - It keeps the call in the "fix the call" group of `ToolErrors.hpp`, where `unknown_tool` already put it.
  - `not_found` means "read the state again, then call again", and re-reading the workspace cannot find an attachment.
  - The "Ask the person" codes (`opened_before`, `workspace_unavailable`) mean other conditions.
  - The message names the step.
- **Side effect.** A model attached in an earlier message of the chat can now be imported later, because the resolver looks the id up in the whole document.

**Tests.**

- `test_agent_bridge.cpp`, "the tool list is the same on every request of a chat, whatever a message attaches". It runs on the real host with the Anthropic wire format:
  - turn 1 has no attachment
  - turn 2 attaches a model and imports it, adding one object
  - turn 3 calls `object_import` with an id that names nothing
  - all 5 requests carry byte-identical `tools`, `object_import` included
  - the turn-3 call comes back as an `is_error` result with `invalid_arguments` and the message, and adds no object
- **Proved fail-first.** I temporarily put back the old rule (offer `object_import` only with an importable attachment), rebuilt and ran the test. It failed 5 of 28 assertions: the attachment turn's two requests carried a different tool list, and the turn-3 call got `unknown_tool`. I then restored the source.
- `test_tool_coordinator.cpp`: the unresolvable-attachment case now expects `invalid_arguments` and the exact message.
- `test_openai_responses_agent.cpp`: the tool list with a model attachment equals the list without one.
- Updated counts: from 29 to 30 tools in three tests.

**Knock-on changes outside the Agent sources.** Both are generated or test files, and both follow directly from the change:

- **`tests/project_prompt/project_tools.json`.**
  - Regenerated with `JUSPRIN_UPDATE_PROJECT_TOOLS=1`: 31 tools, 39,661 bytes compact, up from 38,792 (+869).
  - The README and a comment in `run_prompt_tests.py` were updated to match.
- **`tests/shell/project_prompt_scenario.inc`.**
  - The prompt recorder used to strip `object_import` before comparing a request's tools with `project_tools.json`. It now compares directly.
  - It also leaves `prompt_cache_key` out of recorded bodies; that is commit `c5bd57c8eb`.
  - The file compiles: the object file was built on its own.
  - The harness was **not run**, because that needs a full app build, which I did not start on the shared machine.
  - The shell-harness session (L0, `cache-log`) should know about this change.

**Behaviour change, not evaluated.** Every project-chat request now describes `object_import`, about 870 bytes, including turns with nothing attached. Per the plan's rule, steps that change what the model reads run the prompt evals. **No live evals were run.** That needs Kenneth's approval of a batch.

**Not changed.** `skill_read` is still offered only when the page lists skills. That list is fixed for a host session, and the printer sessions name their own tools, so it does not vary within a chat.

## 3. The Anthropic cache breakpoint and skill text

**Where the breakpoints are today** (`AnthropicCodec.cpp`, all `{"type":"ephemeral"}`):

1. The last tool (`tools_json`, line 87).
2. The single `system` block (`build`, line 272).
3. The last block of the newest `user` message after role normalisation (`build`, line 262). It moves forward on every request.

A fired skill is sent as an in-array `role: "system"` message right after the user content or the tool results that fired it (`push_skills`). Its picture is a user image block, which merges into that user message, so the picture sits before breakpoint 3 and is cached. The skill text sits after it.

- On the request that fires it, the skill text is billed uncached at 1x.
- On the next request of the turn it is written to the cache at 1.25x.

That is M1's leak.

**Bytes after the last breakpoint, 26 recorded bodies.**

- **Method.** Each body was mapped to the Anthropic codec's message layout: developer items become system messages, then the codec's merge and normalisation rules apply. Then I counted the compact JSON after the breakpoint block.
- **Script.** `/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin--claude-worktrees-cache-r8-f275c7/c449884d-06ef-4be3-ae77-8382bf117ba4/scratchpad/r8/after_breakpoint.py`, run as `python3 -I <script> tests/project_prompt/requests.json`.
- **Scope.** The system prompt and tools, about 41 KB, come before breakpoints 1 and 2 and are not counted.

|---|---|---|
| model-imported-by-tool, model-opened-by-tool, model-opened-unnamed | 8,520 each | 8,446 (file-loaded) |
| advice-infill, answer-from-context, direct-change, issue-explain, issue-fix, loaded-vs-configured, reply-in-german, slice-warnings-ready, troubleshoot-first-layer | 5,309 each | 5,210 (print issues) |

##### L0 report
# Request-body logging (L0): report

Untracked working note, 2026-10-29. Branch `claude/cache-request-log-eca52c`, commit `282342b918`, on top of `claude/chat-history-cache` (`cd4162fa97`). Not pushed or merged.

## Problem

The chat-history cache work has to check that each model request opens with the bytes of the one before it. No full request body was kept anywhere. The prompt-test recorder's `requests.json` holds bodies for its own suite, with stored results cut at 4,000 characters, and the live harness modes printed only token counts.

## What I built

- **`tests/jusprin_support/RequestLog.hpp`** (header-only, so the harness and `agent_bridge_tests` share it with no CMake change). `RequestLog::transport(provider, inner)` wraps any `IAgentHttpTransport`; `RequestLog::agent(inner)` wraps any `IAgentService`, so the log knows each request's purpose (reply or title), request id and attempt. For the n-th request of a run it writes:
  - `NNNN-request.json`: the body exactly as the transport was given it, written before it is forwarded.
  - `NNNN-request.meta.json`: provider, URL, headers (`Authorization`, `x-api-key` and other credential headers redacted; `Idempotency-Key` kept), project id and chat id (chat ids restart in each project), purpose, request id, attempt, post time, body length.
  - `NNNN-response.sse`: the response stream as received.
  - `NNNN-response.json`: outcome (complete, error, cancelled, replaced, not_started), HTTP status, usage with the provider's own field names (Anthropic `cache_read_input_tokens`/`cache_creation_input_tokens` come through as-is), stop reason, assembled text, error. It reads both the Messages and the Responses stream.
- **Shell harness flag `--request-log <dir>`**, for `--live-agent`, `--manual-live-agent` and `--project-prompt-requests`. It refuses a non-empty directory and any other mode (exit 2). Documented in the header comment of `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp` (where all flags are documented; there is no `tests/shell/README.md`) and in a new section of `tests/project_prompt/README.md`.
- **`tests/project_prompt/prefix_check.py LOG_DIR [--ignore-key KEY] [--json]`**. For consecutive requests of the same project, chat and purpose it reports the common byte prefix, the first differing byte, the JSON path of that byte in each body, and the path of the last differing byte. `[append]` means the later body is the earlier one with items added at the end of one array and every other byte unchanged. `--ignore-key cache_control` drops Anthropic's moving breakpoint (then the bodies are compared as Python re-serialises them, and the output says so). Unit tests: `tests/project_prompt/test_prefix_check.py`.

## How I verified it

- **Catch2** `[request-log]` in `tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp` (appended at the end): two turns on the real host and provider loop, once per wire format, against the existing `RecordingProvider` fake. Each logged reply body equals the bytes the fake received; usage, stop reason, text, project and chat id, numbering and redaction are checked. I proved it can fail: making the logger append one byte to each body gave 4 byte-equality failures and 8 length failures; restored, it passes (150 assertions).
- **Whole agent suite**: 471 test cases, 16,575 assertions, all passed (Release build in this worktree).
- **`test_prefix_check.py`**: 9 tests pass. The "an append followed by a later change is not an append" test fails when the tail condition is removed.
- **Scripted harness run**: `--project-prompt-requests` on the `direct` conversation of `script.json` (two passes, scripted model, nothing sent over the network) with `--request-log` wrote 333 requests (1,332 files, largest body 1.4 MB). `prefix_check.py` reported all 329 pairs as `[append]` and took 7 seconds. The recorder's own output file was byte-identical with and without `--request-log`. `requests.json` and the baselines are untouched.

## What I could not verify, and things to know

- **No live run.** No model was called. The Anthropic path is tested only through the Catch2 fake; the Responses path through the fake and the scripted harness run. Real streams (OpenAI's `response.completed` usage, Anthropic's `message_start`/`message_delta` usage) follow the documented shapes the codecs already parse, but no real stream has gone through this logger yet.
- **The live harness mode only builds an OpenAI agent** on this branch. The Anthropic journey mode (`--plan-journey`) is uncommitted in `.claude/worktrees/opus-cost-batch`; to log it, wrap its `make_openai_http_transport()` with `log.transport("anthropic", …)` and its agent with `log.agent(…)`, the same way `install_harness_agent` does.
- **Not logged**: the printer panel's Agent and any agent the host rebuilds through its chat model source (a chat that picks a model other than the one the harness installed). Both are built from the app configuration through `make_openai_http_transport()` in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Covering them needs a small seam in production code (for example a test-settable transport wrapper used by `make_openai_http_transport`); I did not add one.
- **Reading the byte count on OpenAI**: the app writes JSON keys alphabetically, so a Responses body opens with `input` and has `instructions` and `tools` after it. The shared byte count of a clean append is then just the earlier `input`; read the kind and the last-difference path, not the count. This is about the JSON byte order only. The order the provider caches in is its own and was not checked here.
- **Pre-existing harness failures, unrelated to this change**: the scripted run of the `direct` conversation reports `direct-change_ends_with_print-issues FAIL` and `direct-change_sent_once_0 FAIL`, with and without `--request-log`. The cause is not investigated; it means `script.json`'s expectation that the `direct-change` point carries the print-issues skill no longer holds on `claude/chat-history-cache`. Re-recording `requests.json` from this branch would hit it.
- The Catch2 fake sends a second chat-title request after the second reply. That is host behaviour with this fake (the title answer is not taken), not the logger's; the test does not pin the title count.

- 15 of 26 bodies have bytes after the breakpoint, totalling 81,950. In every case it is one trailing system message holding the skill.
- With a breakpoint on the skill it would be 0 in every case.

**Why I did not move the breakpoint.** Source: Anthropic's mid-conversation system messages page (`platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-system-messages`), read 2026-10-29.

- **Under R2 it is an error.** R2 sends skills as turn-scoped messages (`clear_at: "next_user_message"`). The page says such a message carries "no `cache_control`" ("A cleared message is never part of a cache key, so a breakpoint on it could never match"). The API answers `cache_control is not permitted on a turn-scoped system message` with a 400. It says to "Put the breakpoint on the last block of the preceding user turn instead". Its agent-loop example puts it on the last `tool_result`. That is exactly today's breakpoint 3.
- **Today it is undocumented.** For a plain (`clear_at: "never"`) system message, the page says it "is itself cacheable", and that on the next turn "you can move your cache breakpoint past it". It never says `cache_control` is allowed on its blocks. Verifying that would need a live call, so I made none.

The rule was to change the placement only if it is right under both today's behaviour and R2's. Moving the breakpoint onto the skill is right under neither for certain, and is a 400 under R2. The code is unchanged.

**Recommendation for R2.**

1. **Keep breakpoint 3 where it is**, on the last block of the newest user message, which is the user turn before any skill. Never put `cache_control` on a turn-scoped message.
2. **The leak goes away under R2 without a breakpoint change.** The page says a turn-scoped message "renders only while no `role: "user"` message comes after it" and "A user message that carries only `tool_result` blocks counts". A cleared message "costs no input tokens".
   - So under R2 a skill's text is billed once, on the request that fires it, and is never written to the cache.
   - Today the same text is billed at 1x, then written at 1.25x, then read on the turn's later requests.
   - The 81,950 bytes above stay after the breakpoint on the firing request, but stop being written to the cache one request late.
3. **The clearing request reads the right entry.** The page says that on the request that clears a message, "the reusable cached prefix ends at the user turn before it, so only the one assistant turn between that message and the new user message is reprocessed". The entry it reads is the one breakpoint 3 wrote on the firing request. That is another reason not to move breakpoint 3.
4. **A design point R2 must settle (behaviour, not cost).** Because a `tool_result` message clears a turn-scoped message, the model sees the skill only on the request that fired it, not "for the rest of the turn".
   - That matches what the Responses codec does today, since it drops the skill from the next request.
   - It does not match today's Anthropic codec, which keeps the skill visible for the rest of the turn.
   - If the plan's "cleared at the next user message" meant the next message from the person, `clear_at` does not do that.
5. **A message after a tool result on smaller models.** The plan already notes that Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 may ignore a system message placed right after a tool result. Under R2 that is the only place a skill fired by a result can go.

**TTL (decision D7).** Confirmed: the codec sends no `ttl`. `ephemeral()` is `{"type":"ephemeral"}` at all three breakpoints, so the 5-minute default applies. Nothing in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/` mentions `ttl` or `1h`. The gateway forwards `cache_control` unchanged.

- **The shell harness.** The `--project-prompt-requests` path with the new tool comparison was compiled but not run.
- **Effect on answers.** Whether always offering `object_import` changes any answers. No live evals were run.

**What each one delivered**

- **Deletions (R1 + R3a)** on `refs/heads/claude/cache-r1-r3a-7264fd`, two commits. Production diff is +1/−104 lines in `AgentHost.cpp`, all deletion. The agent suite passes. The guard test fails at the same count, as expected, but its first failure moved from the reminder to the workspace block and picture, which is what the next steps address.
- **Cache hygiene (R8)** on `refs/heads/claude/cache-r8-f275c7`, three commits. Production diff is +28/−10 across eight files: a `chat_key` carried from host to codec, `prompt_cache_key` sent on OpenAI and OpenRouter, `object_import` offered on every turn with a clean `invalid_arguments` failure when nothing is attached, and the `ImportableAttachment` enum value removed. Fail-first was proven on the tool-list test. The breakpoint was left in place with a written analysis.
- **Request logging (L0)** on `refs/heads/claude/cache-request-log-eca52c`, one commit, test code only. A `--request-log` flag writes each body byte-exact with its response usage, and `prefix_check.py` compares consecutive bodies. A scripted run logged 333 requests and every pair was a clean append.

**Three findings worth your attention**

1. **The JusPrin Cloud gateway refuses `prompt_cache_key`.** The R8 session read the gateway source in `tsd-enterprise` and found an allowlist of Responses fields. The app therefore skips the key for signed-in accounts, which is where it matters most, since every cloud user shares one OpenAI organisation. The fix is a gateway change first (add the field to the allowlist and deploy), then drop the condition in the app. The same reading showed in-array system messages pass through untouched, but client headers do not. R2's `clear_at` beta header has to be configured on the gateway's alias backend or it will fail.
2. **`clear_at` clears earlier than the design assumed.** Anthropic clears a turn-scoped message at the next user-role message, and a tool-result message counts. So under R2 a skill is visible only on the request that fired it, not for the rest of the turn. That matches today's OpenAI path and not today's Anthropic path. This needs a decision before R2 starts; it is recorded in the plan doc.
3. **A harness scenario is already broken on the integration branch.** L0 found two failures in the scripted `direct` conversation with and without its flag. The `direct-change` point no longer carries the print-issues skill. Re-recording `requests.json`, which R1 needs before the injection eval, will hit this.

Merging is mechanical: each branch merges cleanly onto cd4162fa97, and R8 and L0 both appended tests to the end of `test_agent_bridge.cpp`, so one conflict needs a hand resolution. The simplicity table in the plan doc now has the numbers for all three.

Replace the Agent's re-derived history with an append-only per-chat record that is rendered byte for byte on every request, so that the `[history-prefix]` guard passes on both wire formats and can be un-hidden. This is step R7 of the plan, and it carries R2 (skills) and R6 (notes) with it because the three are one model; R4 (workspace blocks) and R5 (pictures) fall out of "keep as sent". Read the plan doc's "Roles and lifetimes", "Gateway findings" and "R2 design point" sections before designing.

What the record is:
- Per chat, bound to one wire format (a chat talks to one provider family; D5: a model switch within the same format is allowed and only costs one cold cache; a switch across formats on an existing chat must be refused in `AgentHost::handle_set_chat_model` with a clear error, not silently re-rendered).
- Every item ever sent to the model, in order, with its exact wire content: the person's messages with what travelled with them (workspace block, plate picture, file report), assistant output including thinking or reasoning exactly as received (Anthropic thinking blocks with signatures; OpenAI reasoning items; check what each codec receives today and what the provider requires to be replayed), tool calls and results, fired skills, app notes.
- A lifetime per item, never an edit. Skills are visible only on the request that fired them (settled: on Anthropic via in-array `role:"system"` with `clear_at: "next_user_message"` and the beta header `mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21`; on OpenAI as a `developer` item that has no clear and simply stays, so keep it as it is). App notes become operator-role in-conversation messages (Anthropic in-array `system`, OpenAI `developer`), kept visible, same for project and printer chats; this replaces the "JusPrin app note, not the person's words" user-text prefix. Tool results stay in their own channel.
- Pictures are stored as attachment-blob references and rendered inline at request time; image bytes never go into `state.json`.
- Stored in the chat document (`ProjectStateDocument`/`ProjectPersistence`), so a reopened project continues its chat with the same bytes. Design the migration for chats recorded before this change honestly: a one-time rendering of the old messages (plain person/assistant text, no tool replay) appended as the chat's first record items, after which nothing is re-derived; do not keep the legacy history builder alive beyond that one path, and say in the commit message what an old chat's model now sees.

Gateway constraint: the JusPrin Cloud gateway forwards messages and `cache_control` untouched but sends only its own configured headers, so the `clear_at` beta header does not reach Anthropic through it yet. Send `clear_at` and the header only when the profile is not `account_sign_in`; for the gateway path skills stay visible as on OpenAI. Make this a per-profile decision, never per-request, so one chat's rendering never changes. Note it in the report as the follow-up the gateway needs (add the header to the alias backend in `JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES`).

What to delete: the history re-derivation in `make_agent_request` (the `calls_by_message` replay of `ToolActivity` records into history entries, the text retelling of assistant replies, the note prefix, the stripping of workspace blocks and pictures, the skill-dropping) and anything that only served it. The expected outcome is less production code than before; if a part grows, say why in its commit message.

Tests: fake transports only (see `RecordingProvider`, `anthropic_stream`, `responses_stream` in `test_agent_bridge.cpp`). Add tests that encode the valid transitions: an item once sent is never changed; a later request is the earlier request plus appended items (for Anthropic, modulo the moving `cache_control` breakpoint on the newest user message; keep breakpoint placement as it is, never on a turn-scoped message); a cross-format switch is refused; an old chat migrates once; a reopened project renders the same bytes. Finally drop the `[.]` from the two guard cases so CTest runs them, and show the guard passing on both wire formats. Run the whole agent suite.

Commits: at least one for the record model and rendering (R7, including R4/R5), one for skill lifetime (R2), one for notes as operator role (R6), one for the cross-format refusal (D5), one un-hiding the guard. Each message says what changed, why, and the production diff direction. Done means: all commits on your branch, agent suite and guard green, and an untracked `r7-report.md` in the worktree root with the design as built, the migration behaviour, the production diff stat, the gateway follow-up, what the model now sees differently (this is a behaviour change and will be evaluated live later; list every difference), and anything unverified.

- **Bad:** `434e893a6b`. The same script gives `HARNESS RESULT FAIL failures=12`, and so does `jusprin-newui` HEAD plus the integration commits, as the table shows.

**First bad commit: `434e893a6b`.** It adds a fork-owned table, `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/SliceResultWarnings.cpp`, which classifies the bed-temperature warning as never shown:

```cpp
        // The dialog never names it.
        {BED_TEMP_TOO_HIGH_THAN_FILAMENT, Shown::Never, false},
```

`PrintIssueMonitor::read_result` reads the slice warnings for the chip, and the workspace's `sliceWarnings` come from that reader. It used to keep every warning that has words:

```cpp
-        for (const GCodeProcessorResult::SliceWarning& warning : result->warnings) {
-            ...
-            if (text.empty())
-                continue; // OrcaSlicer has no words for it and shows nothing itself
```

Now it keeps only the warnings the table shows `Always`:

```cpp
+        for (const std::size_t index : Workspace::shown_slice_result_warnings(kinds)) {
+            const GCodeProcessorResult::SliceWarning& warning = result->warnings[index];
+            if (Workspace::slice_result_warning_shown(warning.msg) != Workspace::SliceResultWarningShown::Always)
+                continue;
```

`slice_report` already left the bed-temperature warning out before this commit. What changed is the chip's reader, and with it the workspace's `sliceWarnings`. `AgentHost::fire_print_issues` (`AgentHost.cpp:1159`) fires only for a plate whose `slice_warnings` sequence is new. The fixture plate now has no `slice_warnings`, so nothing fires.

The change was deliberate. The commit message says the chip used to count "the bed-temperature warning, which OrcaSlicer raises on every PLA print and never shows in its own window". The same commit:

- deletes the heatbed row from `AgentUI/src/skills/print-issues/SKILL.md`
- adds `CHECK(slice_result_warning_shown(BED_TEMP_TOO_HIGH_THAN_FILAMENT) == SliceResultWarningShown::Never)` to the new `tests/jusprin/test_slice_result_warnings.cpp`
- updates `tests/shell/print_issues_scenario.inc` for the removed "Resolve with AI" button

It touches nothing under `tests/project_prompt/`.

## Process gap

**Why no test failed at `434e893a6b`.** The only check that ties "the fixture's slice warns" to "these six points carry the skill" is the prompt recorder, `--project-prompt-requests`. It runs only by hand, when someone re-records. Nothing in CMake/ctest, `.github` or the scripts runs it. A full run takes about 28 minutes on this Mac. The commit's own verification was the Catch2 suites and the `print_issues` shell scenario, and both pass, because neither depends on the bed-temperature warning reaching the agent.

**Why `requests.json` did not show it.** The file is a snapshot: whatever was last recorded stays there until someone records again. The README says so: "Nothing checks that `requests.json` stays current: record it again when a tool's results, the fixture or the request shape change". It also says "A skill edit therefore needs a new recording". `434e893a6b` edited the print-issues SKILL.md and changed the request shape for six points, and it did not re-record.

The last whole recording is `9d05d60eaf` (Windows, 2026-10-25); the last partial one is `8a70ea68bd` (2026-10-26). So since 2026-10-28, `run_prompt_tests.py` has been sending, for those six cases, requests the app no longer builds: a bed-temperature `sliceWarnings` and the old print-issues skill text. Any live batch since then measured the model on those old requests. The README note at line 343 ("Since 2026-10-18 the slice summary counts every warning the print-issue chip lists, OrcaSlicer's bed-temperature warning … included") has been false since that commit.

**Catch2 coverage.** `tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp` has a print-issues skill section (from line 4682). Its cases include:

- "warnings from the person's slice fire the print-issues skill on the next request only, once per new set"
- "a chip's message with new warnings carries the print-issues skill once"
- "warnings from a slice that ends while the model's call runs fire the print-issues skill on that result"

They all inject warnings with `set_plate_warnings_for_testing`, so they cover the firing logic, which is unchanged and still correct. No Catch2 case slices a real plate and checks which OrcaSlicer warnings reach the workspace. The table's own test asserts the new behaviour, the bed-temperature warning never shown, which is correct for the app. Nothing records that the prompt suite depended on the old behaviour.

**The order dependency.** Running a subset of `script.json` changes the fixture without any message: conversations after `prepare` inherit its Textured PEI plate. The README documents this at lines 360-361. The recorder does not check it, so a run of `direct` alone looks like a regression when it is not.

**What would have caught it.** Any of these:

Separately, the recorder could select each conversation's plate itself, or refuse a script that omits `prepare` for points that need its plate. Then a subset run would not fail for the wrong reason.

## Brief changed after the work was done

After all four pieces were finished, the session that started this one changed the brief. The new brief said: don't investigate or fix the `direct-change` failure (a separate session owns it), leave `script.json` as it is, don't bisect, and record as-is. I didn't bisect. But `4d663df65c` (the `script.json` change plus a README paragraph) was already committed. I haven't reverted it: undoing a commit needs Kenneth's confirmation.

Recording as-is, with the original script: the recorder reports 12 failing checks (`HARNESS RESULT FAIL failures=12`), but it still writes the file (`prompt_requests_written PASS`). That file matches the committed `requests.json` once timestamps, temp paths and picture bytes are normalised; none of the 26 cases differs. So the step 2 commit is what the unchanged recorder produces, with or without `4d663df65c`. The `direct-change` body's difference from the old recording: `input[1]` (the print-issues skill) is gone, so `once` is no longer set (it was 1); the plate's `sliceWarnings` (the bed-temperature warning) is gone from the `<workspace>` block; and the revision number is lower.

## 1. The scripted `direct` failure was a deliberate change; the script was stale

**Problem.** The scripted recorder run (`--project-prompt-requests`, no model) failed on more than `direct`. On the whole script it failed 12 checks: `_ends_with_print-issues` and `_sent_once_0` for six points, all on the two-plate fixture and all sending a typed message: `advice-infill`, `reply-in-german`, `troubleshoot-first-layer`, `answer-from-context`, `loaded-vs-configured`, `direct-change`. The L0 session had run only `direct`, so it saw two of them. Log: `m4-openai-baseline/evidence/step1-before-fix-harness.log`.

**Cause.** The print-issues skill is added to the first request after a plate gets slice warnings the model hasn't seen (`AgentHost::fire_print_issues`, which reads `plates[].slice_warnings` in the workspace snapshot), or after a press on a print-issue chip. The fixture's sliced plate (Bambu PLA Basic, X1 Carbon) has exactly one slice warning: OrcaSlicer's bed-temperature warning. `434e893a6b` ("Show the same slice warnings on the issue chip, to the agent and in Check print", 2026-10-28, on `jusprin-newui`) made the chip, and with it the workspace block, show only the warnings OrcaSlicer's send dialog shows. `Workspace/SliceResultWarnings.cpp` marks `BED_TEMP_TOO_HIGH_THAN_FILAMENT` as `Never`, and the commit message names this exact warning as the one it meant to drop ("which OrcaSlicer raises on every PLA print and never shows in its own window"). So the six points no longer get the sk

**Evidence.**
- The old recording (2026-10-25/26) has `sliceWarnings` with "The current hot bed temperature is relatively high…" in all six bodies. A fresh run has no `sliceWarnings` and no skill in any of them. The chip-press points (`issue-fix`, `issue-explain`) and the overhang fixture's `slice-warnings-ready` still carry the skill.
- The L0 harness binary at `282342b918` (this branch before R1 and R8) passes the fixed script with 0 failures. So the cache-programme commits (R1, R3a, R8, L0) didn't cause the failure; it came with the base `953eddb355`.
- Not done: I didn't build the parent of `434e893a6b` to bisect. The code path and the two recordings make the cause direct, and another full build was not worth it.

**Fix.** The six points lose `"skill": "print-issues"`. The README paragraph that explained why they were marked now says why the mark went. The prompt-case batches in `baseline.json` for these six were run with the skill on the request, so the next prompt-case batch is the first one without it for those six.

## 2. `requests.json` recorded again

The committed file was a Windows recording from 2026-10-25, with four skill texts copied in from macOS on 10-26. The new file is a whole macOS recording from this branch. I compared the two with `evidence/compare_recordings.py`. It normalises the known run-to-run noise: ISO timestamps, the harness's temp directory and project id, and `view_render` PNG bytes. It also parses `<workspace>` blocks and JSON tool results, so a change shows up as a JSON path. The outputs are in `evidence/step2-*.txt`.

**The three expected changes, all present:**
- `file-note-not-instructions`: the reminder item at `input[0]` is gone (R1, `e8043e2d7d`). The body now opens with the file-load report: 4 → 3 items.
- `model-imported-by-tool`: no tool list of its own any more. Every request now offers `object_import` (R8, `23cfa48bd1`), so its tools equal `project_tools.json`, and the recorder leaves them out as it does for every other point.
- The six points from step 1 have no `sliceWarnings` and no print-issues skill (`once` 1 → none). Later points on the same fixture (`after-*`, `direct-change-applied`/`-failed`, `first-person`) also lose the warning from their workspace blocks and results.

**Other changes, and why:**
- Skill wording from 2026-10-28: the print-issues skill says "pressed Ask AI" (`issue-fix`, `issue-explain`, `slice-warnings-ready`; `434e893a6b`). The setup skill in `after-intent` has the new text about the setup card's mark (`c7e62ba4f8`).
- Windows differences gone: Windows file paths, `fitsSelectedBed` false → true on the file-load points (a Windows-only fit-check bug, per the README), and OrcaSlicer's English catalog wording in the slice refusal ("not suggested for use printing filament").
- Slice figures (grams, cost, print time) differ slightly in the fourth or fifth digit.
- Revision numbers are about 10% lower throughout, and so are the handles that embed them (`f118-…` → `f106-…`); `calibration-symptom`'s object ids are shifted. **Not attributed to a commit.** Against the L0-harness recording from today they are identical, so they come from the Windows recording or from `jusprin-newui` commits between 10-25 and 10-28. I didn't separate the two.
- R3a (`a26e25bd47`, 16 KiB result cut removed) changes no body: the largest replayed result in any recording is 10,440 bytes.

**Branch-only diff.** Against a recording made by the L0 harness (`282342b918`) with the same fixed script, only three cases differ: the two R1/R8 items above, and `after-slice`'s recorded answers (next point).

**Recorder noise worth knowing.** In `after-slice`, each recorded `slice_report` answer is either a full report or `valid:false`, depending on whether the scripted slice finished before the answer was taken. Two runs of the same build differ this way, and so does the L0 harness. It affects answers only, not request bodies. Not fixed (out of scope).

**With and without `--request-log`.** The two files are **not byte-identical**, and neither are any two runs: stored tool results carry `updatedAt` timestamps and temp paths. After normalisation the run with `--request-log` equals the run without it, with no case differing (`step2-without-vs-with-request-log.txt`). Two runs without the flag differ only in the `after-slice` answers noise (`step2-run-vs-run.txt`). The committed file is the run without the flag. `baseline.json` is untouched. `test_steps.py` changed in two places: its list of points that send something once loses the six, and one comment no longer mentions the bed-temperature warning.

Note: `test_steps.py` needs the `tool_call_check` binary built (`--target tool_call_check`). Without it, 29 of its 50 tests fail on the unchanged branch.

## 3. Journey mode ported, on both providers, with request logging

`--plan-journey <model-file> <exchange-directory>` is ported from the uncommitted diff in `opus-cost-batch`. The turn loop and the `turn-N.json` writer are unchanged. Nothing from that worktree's `src/` was ported. What changed from that diff:

- The Agent is built the way the app builds one for a saved key: `make_provider_agent` with the provider row's codec and the app's HTTP transport, for both providers. `JUSPRIN_JOURNEY_PROVIDER` = `openai` (the default, with `OPENAI_API_KEY`) or `anthropic` (with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`). `JUSPRIN_JOURNEY_MODEL` sets the model; `JUSPRIN_AGENT_ENDPOINT` sets the endpoint.
- The old OpenAI path went through an OpenRouter host-pinning transport that also stripped every picture. I dropped it, because a cost baseline has to send what the app sends.
- `--request-log` works in this mode. The transport and agent are wrapped with `RequestLog` as `install_harness_agent` does for the other modes, and the log records the right provider id.
- The usage line has one shape on both providers and always includes `cache_creation_tokens` (0 on OpenAI).

**How it was verified, with no paid call:** I ran a local fake provider (`evidence/fake_provider.py`) that streams OpenAI Responses and Anthropic Messages events: one `workspace_inspect` call, then a text reply, per turn. I ran one OpenAI journey (vase) and one Anthropic journey (plug), each a file load plus one message, then `END`. Each produced 5 requests (two per turn plus the chat title), all logged with the right provider and URL and with usage. Both got HARNESS RESULT PASS, and `prefix_check.py` reads both logs. `--request-log` with an unsupported mode (`--mcp`) still exits 2. The fake runs are in `evidence/fake-journeys/`.

## 4. M4: OpenAI `gpt-5.4-mini` three-chat baseline (one approved run)

I used the same three chats as the Opus baseline (`opus-batch/out-baseline/`). The models were `Spiral_Vase1_SOLID.STL`, `OrcaPlug_v2.drc` and `Stanford_Bunny.drc`, and the messages were read from that run's `next-N.txt` files: vase got two messages, plug and bunny one each. Runs: 2026-10-29 19:47–20:15 UTC, one chat after another, each with `--request-log`. Everything is in `m4-openai-baseline/`: scripts (`start.sh`, `say.sh`, `show.py`, `cost.py`), and `out/<chat>/` with `harness.log`, `turn-N.json`, `request-log/` and `prefix_check.txt`. All three runs got HARNESS RESULT PASS.

**Prices used:** OpenAI's standard tier for gpt-5.4-mini: $0.75 per 1M input tokens, $0.075 per 1M cached input tokens, $4.50 per 1M output tokens. I read them on 2026-10-29 at `developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing`; the model page `developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.4-mini` gives the same figures. Cached tokens are a part of input tokens, so cost = (input − cached) × 0.75 + cached × 0.075 + output × 4.50, per million.

| Chat | Requests (reply + title) | Input tokens | Cached input | Cached share | Output tokens | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| vase | 10 (8 + 2) | 98,828 | 66,048 | 66.8% | 1,126 | $0.0346 |
| plug | 6 (5 + 1) | 53,618 | 28,032 | 52.3% | 872 | $0.0252 |
| bunny | 7 (6 + 1) | 78,922 | 50,816 | 64.4% | 916 | $0.0290 |
| **total** | **23** | **231,368** | **144,896** | **62.6%** | **2,914** | **$0.0888** |

Reasoning tokens were 0 on every request (why is not checked). The request-log totals match the harness's `JUSPRIN LIVE USAGE` lines exactly. For scale only: the Opus 5.5 baseline of the same chats cost $1.29 (40 usage lines, 914 K input tokens), but its turns took different paths, so the two runs can't be compared request by request.

**Prefix check** (`prefix_check.py`, reply requests per chat, consecutive pairs):

| Chat | Pairs | Clean appends | Changed: first differing path → what it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| vase | 7 | 4 (2→3, 4→5, 7→8, 8→9) | 1→2 `$.input[0].content`; 3→4 `$.input[7].content`; 5→7 `$.input[2].content` |
| plug | 4 | 2 (2→3, 4→5) | 1→2 `$.input[0].content`; 3→4 `$.input[9].content` |
| bunny | 5 | 3 (2→3, 4→5, 5→6) | 1→2 `$.input[0].content`; 3→4 `$.input[7].content` |
| **total** | **16** | **9** | **7** |

The one title pair (vase 6 → 10) is identical. The seven changed pairs are of three kinds, all on the plan's list:

- **Turn start after the file load** (1→2 in every chat; R4, R5, R2). The file-load report at `input[0]` goes from a two-part content (report plus `<workspace>` block) to a plain string. The plate picture at `input[1]` and the file-loaded skill at `input[2]` are dropped.
- **Turn start of a later turn** (vase 5→7; R4). The person's earlier message at `input[2]` loses its `<workspace>` block and becomes a plain string.
- **Skill dropped on the next request** (3→4 in every chat; R2). The setup-changed skill (a `developer` message) is in the request that fired it and gone from the next, where a `function_call` takes its place.

Caching follows these rewrites. The first request of each chat has 0 cached tokens. The second request (the first one after a rewrite) also has 0 cached in all three chats (8,818 / 8,783 / 8,771 input). Requests after a clean append cache from about 8,700 tokens up to nearly the whole input (vase 9: 14,720 of 15,079).

**Things in this run to know before using it as the baseline:**
- **The vase chat paused 22 minutes between its two messages.** The Opus baseline did not. Turn 1 finished at 19:50:30 UTC, but my driver only wrote the second message at 20:12:58, and at 19:50:20 the chat-title request failed with `Could not resolve host: api.openai.com`, so the Mac's network or this session stalled. The first request after the pause (vase 7) still had 7,936 of 11,950 tokens cached. The app asked for the title again later (vase 10), and that worked.
- gpt-5.4-mini made four calls the app refused as `invalid_arguments`: vase `settings_preview_patch`, plug `settings_search` and `settings_preview_patch`, bunny `object_place`. Every chat still ended normally. I didn't judge answer quality.
- **Logger quirk (L0's `RequestLog`):** 7 of 23 responses are written with `outcome: "replaced"` and `status: 0` even though the stream finished (`stop: "completed"`, usage present). The Agent posts its next request before the transport's HTTP-complete event arrives, so the log closes the response as replaced. Token numbers aren't affected. Worth fixing so that `status` reads 200.
- No API key is in any stored file: I searched `m4-openai-baseline/` and the scratchpad for the key and for key-shaped strings, and found none. The scripts source the key from `~/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env` inside a subshell and never print it.

## Not verified

- Which commit lowered the revision numbers (Windows recording versus `jusprin-newui` commits, step 2).
- No bisect build at the parent of `434e893a6b` (step 1). The cause rests on the code path, the two recordings and the L0-harness run.
- Why the second request of each OpenAI chat has 0 cached tokens, when the instructions and tools it shares with the first request come before any rewritten item. My guess is that OpenAI doesn't start cache hits until a prefix has been seen and written, or that the first request's large picture changes how the prefix is hashed. That is a guess, not checked against OpenAI's documentation.
- The Anthropic journey path is proved only against the fake. No live Anthropic run was made, because it was not approved.

Three results are in. The R7 diff is with an independent reviewer; I will not ask about merging until that comes back. Statements only below, no decisions yet.

**Regression investigation (the card you started).** The cause is commit 434e893a6b from 2026-10-28, a deliberate change: the issue chip, and with it the workspace block the model reads, now lists only the slice warnings OrcaSlicer's own dialog shows, and the bed-temperature warning is marked never shown. That warning was the prompt fixture's only warning, so six prompt-suite cases stopped receiving the print-issues skill. The parent commit passes, that commit fails 12 checks. Separately, running the `direct` conversation alone fails on every commit because only the `prepare` conversation selects the Textured PEI plate. The process gap: the prompt recorder is the only check that ties the fixture's warnings to those cases, it runs by hand and takes 28 minutes, nothing checks that `requests.json` stays current, and the commit edited the skill text without re-recording. Since 2026-10-28 every prompt-case run has sent six requests the app no longer builds. The full report is `skill-regression-report.md` in the investigation's worktree.

**Harness session.** Re-recorded `requests.json` on the cache branch, ported the three-chat journey mode to both providers with request logging, and ran the one approved OpenAI baseline. One thing you should know: before my instruction to leave the regression alone reached it, it had already committed the fix that drops the skill expectation from the six cases. It did not revert that commit, correctly, since reverting needs your word. The M4 numbers:

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| Requests, three chats | 23 |
| Cached share of input | 62.6% |
| Cost | $0.0888 |
| Consecutive pairs that were clean appends | 9 of 16 |

The seven rewrites are exactly the three leaks R7 removes, so the "after" run should show them gone.

**R7.** Five commits: the record, skill clearing, notes as operator messages, the cross-format refusal, and the guard un-hidden and passing on both wire formats. Production code grew by 361 lines net, which is the opposite of what we expected. The author's accounting: storage of the record and handing settled items from the agent loop to the host are new, while the codecs shrank. Whether that growth is necessary is the main thing the reviewer is checking.

<result>I found two bugs that would leave existing chats permanently unusable in the shipped app, and two more that can do the same. The growth is only partly justified. I read the code at `claude/cache-r7-record-e80b27` without building or running anything, so every finding below comes from reading. Line numbers are on that branch.

### 1. Correctness

1. **Every chat migrated from before this change throws on its first request.** `start_chat_record` stores the migrated items with `format: ""`. On the very next line of the same turn, `ProviderAgent::begin_transcript` (`ProviderAgent.cpp:239-241`) throws `logic_error` because `format != wire_format(family)`. It only checks that the item list is non-empty, not that the format is non-empty. That covers every chat that has an earlier reply with text, on both providers. The exception leaves `begin_stream` with `m_stream` still set and goes to GUI_App's handler. The same throw then happens on every later message in that chat. The migration test (`test_agent_bridge.cpp` "a chat from before the record…") uses `RecordingAgent` rather than `ProviderAgent`, and even asserts `first.record.format.empty()` with two items. It records exactly the input that crashes the real loop. Fix: compare formats only when the format is non-empty.

2. **The production history cleanup deletes every picture and PDF the record keeps.** Blobs go to `<projects>/<id>/attachments/chat-<conv>/…` (`AgentHost.cpp:2758-2769`). After every model version, `ProjectAutosave::trim_history` (`ProjectAutosave.cpp:433-440`) calls `ProjectVersionStore::prune`. Its last loop (`ProjectVersionStore.cpp:987-993`) removes every file under `attachments/` that is not in the document's `attachments` index or `live_attachments`. Chat-record blobs are in neither.
   - After that, `load_record_bytes` (`AgentHost.cpp:2829`) gets `""` back from `read_attachment_blob`, which returns empty for a missing file (`ProjectPersistence.cpp:522-533`).
   - It then sends an image or document block with empty data. Because the record is append-only, every later request in that chat fails.
   - The "reopened project" test runs on in-memory persistence and never touches the version store.
   - A forked managed identity (`ProjectPersistence.cpp:318-333`) copies only the attachment folder from the opened file's auxiliary directory. The old project's managed `chat-*` blobs are not carried over.

3. **A request is recorded when the transport takes it, not when the provider accepts it.** `post()` calls `record()` as soon as `m_transport->post` returns true (`ProviderAgent.cpp:406`). By then the person's message, workspace block, pictures and PDFs are all in the record (see `m_settled` at :257/:300).
   - If the provider then answers 413 (`request_too_large`), or 400 for a bad or oversized image or PDF, that chat can never send again.
   - Before this change, earlier turns' attachments were stripped, so a bad attachment broke only its own turn.
   - The loop test "a turn whose request fails" asserts that the message is kept after a failure. It treats a 503 and a 400/413 the same, so this case is encoded as valid.
   - There is no size limit and no way to recover. Context or size overflow in a long chat (workspace block per turn, every picture, thinking blocks) is the same permanent failure, with only a generic error shown.

4. **Responses reasoning items are now replayed across turns with `store:false`.** They go back with their ids and no `encrypted_content` (`ResponsesCodec.cpp:72-76`, `:155`; no `include` is requested). Community reports describe a 404 "Item … not found. Items are not persisted when store is set to false" for exactly this. If that is right, the failure is now permanent per chat (append-only) instead of one turn. This is unverified against a live API and the author lists it as unverified, but it needs a live check before merge, not after.

5. **Retrying a failed reply that is not the newest sends a request that ends on the assistant.** In `make_agent_request` (`AgentHost.cpp:2967`), `request.source.empty()` returns early. `turn_recorded` (`ProviderAgent.cpp:263`) adds nothing. So the request is the record plus skills, and the record ends with a later turn's assistant item. `handle_retry` does not check that the retried message is the newest. On Anthropic this is an assistant prefill, which some models reject; on Responses it asks for a reply to nothing. Before this change, a retry always ended on the person's words.

6. **`turn_recorded` re-derives "already sent" from `attempt > 1 && source.empty()`.** The host already knows this exactly through `sent(user->id)`. These are two separate decisions about one fact, and only the host's is grounded in the record. Pass the fact, or have the host leave out the workspace.

7. **A rewritten note is sent again only when it starts the turn.** The `rewritten` check (`AgentHost.cpp:2892`) runs only for `user`. A rewritten note elsewhere in the chat is skipped by `sent()` in the unsent loop. Each re-send also appends a duplicate id to `messages` (`ProjectStateDocument.cpp:902`).

8. **Persistence costs grow per turn.** Each turn start parses the whole record three times: `start_record_of_earlier_chat`, `record_refusal`, `make_agent_request`. It also re-reads and base64-encodes every blob the chat ever sent, synchronously on the GUI thread. `publish_document` re-parses and re-dumps the whole state on every write. Attachments are stored twice, once as the attachment and once as a chat blob, and could be referenced instead.

Byte-exactness of rendering, the double-append and skipped-item paths, and thread safety: no finding. Rendering depends only on the record and the profile, the `m_recorded`/`m_settled` bookkeeping is sound, and everything runs on the GUI thread.

### 2. Error-handling discipline

9. **A missing blob silently becomes an empty picture.** `load_record_bytes` relies on `read_attachment_blob`'s "missing file returns empty". That turns a violated invariant into a silent wrong request, and it is what makes finding 2 invisible until the provider rejects it.

10. **The record is written strictly but read leniently.** In `ProjectStateDocument.cpp:92-104`, `record_part_from` treats any non-text, non-image entry as a PDF and defaults `blob`/`mime` to `""`. Meanwhile `record_part_json` throws on an empty blob, and `record_item_from` throws on an unknown kind. Reading should use `at()` and throw on an unknown part kind. `chat_record` has the same leniency with `value("format"/"messages")`.

11. **A reply request with no record sink silently keeps nothing.** In `ProviderAgent::record()` (:329), `!m_on_recorded` is a quiet no-op for replies. That is an invariant violation, since only titles may lack a sink.

12. **Fallible disk I/O runs after the request is already in flight.** The blob-write failure is thrown from inside `on_recorded` (`AgentHost.cpp:2768`), which `post()` calls after dispatch. The exception unwinds through `start()`/`poll()` and leaves `m_busy` true with a live request and `m_stream` set. Propagating is fine; the ordering is the problem.

13. **The same format invariant is checked in three layers.** `record_refusal` in the host, `begin_transcript` in the agent, and `append_chat_record` in the document. Keep the document's check and the host's refusal, and drop the agent's or make it the only pre-send check. The duplication also hid finding 1, because the three disagree on what an empty format means.

### 3. Growth that is not needed (about 70–90 production lines)

14. **The migration duplicates the unsent classification.** `start_record_of_earlier_chat` repeats the file-report / user / note if-chain and the literal report string (`AgentHost.cpp:2816` vs `:2887`). Merging them saves about 15 lines.

15. **`record.messages` mostly duplicates the item `source` fields.** Store only the ids the migration covered and derive the rest from the items. That saves about 10 lines and removes the duplicate data in state.json. `start_chat_record` is `append_chat_record` with an empty format plus covered ids, so merging them saves about 12 lines.

16. **Two parallel traversals.** The `keep` lambda and `load_record_bytes` walk the same parts and result images. One `for_each_blob(items, fn)` saves about 8 lines. Holding raw bytes in `RecordPart` would also drop the base64 encode/decode/re-encode round trip.

17. **The host and the agent split building the person's side.** The host builds `AgentUnsentMessage` plus `source`, `note`, `user_text` and `issue_context`, and the agent turns them into `RecordItem`s (`ProviderAgent.cpp:243-307`). The host could hand over ready-made items and let the agent add only the workspace and skills. That deletes `AgentUnsentMessage`, two request fields and about 25 agent lines. It also deletes the test-side copy of that logic in `kept_turn.hpp` (76 lines), which already differs from production: it keeps `issue_context` untagged, where production wraps it in `<print_issue>`.

18. **Unreachable fallbacks after exhaustive switches** in `record_kind_name`, `part_block` and `input_part`. These are small.

### 4. Test quality

19. Most new tests pin today's ordering and output rather than the transitions that matter. Untested:
    - the real `ProviderAgent` given a migrated record (finding 1);
    - on-disk persistence through autosave and prune (finding 2);
    - a 4xx after acceptance, and what the next turn sends (finding 3);
    - a host-level retry after the record holds the message: `RetryingAgent` never calls `on_recorded`;
    - a stop or failure followed by a new turn under the history-prefix guard (the guard scripts only successful turns);
    - retrying a failed reply that is not the newest.

    The fakes built on `kept_turn.hpp` produce records the real loop would never produce, so the host tests can pass while production differs.

**Verdict:** The storage and settlement code is inherent and justified (roughly the +226 and +73). About 70–90 lines are duplication. The record also brings in permanent per-chat failure modes (findings 1–4) that the old rebuild could not have, and these need fixing before the growth question matters.

Sources for finding 4 (community reports, not official docs):
- [`store: false` breaks multi-turn computer-use](https://community.openai.com/t/store-false-breaks-multi-turn-computer-use/1375928)
- [Item "not found" with store false (Playground File Search thread)](https://community.openai.com/t/using-openai-playground-web-platform-to-test-responses-api-with-file-search-results-in-error/1354943)
- [Reasoning item provided without its required following item](https://community.openai.com/t/how-to-solve-badrequesterror-400-item-rs-of-type-reasoning-was-provided-without-its-required-following-item-error-in-responses-api/1151686)</result>
