input.message:
Independent review of claude/cache-r7-record-e80b27 found four problems that block merging; three I confirmed by reading your branch. Please fix them on your branch, each with a test that fails first, and report back. Keep the record model; this is a rework of its edges, not a redesign.

1. CONFIRMED. Every migrated chat throws on its first request. start_chat_record stores the migrated record with format "" (ProjectStateDocument.cpp:916). ProviderAgent::begin_transcript (ProviderAgent.cpp:239) throws logic_error whenever items are non-empty and format != wire_format(family), so "" fails on both providers, on that message and every later one. The migration test uses RecordingAgent, not ProviderAgent, and asserts the empty format, so it records exactly the input that crashes the real loop. Fix: the migration stamps the turn's wire format (it already knows it), and the test runs the real ProviderAgent with a fake transport over a migrated chat. While there, the same format invariant is checked in three layers (record_refusal in the host, begin_transcript in the agent, append_chat_record in the document); keep the document's check plus the host's refusal and drop the agent's, per AGENTS.md "no duplicated defensive checks".

2. CONFIRMED. The version-store prune deletes every picture and PDF the record keeps. Blobs go to attachments/chat-<conv>/<request>-<n> (ProjectStateDocument.hpp:114, AgentHost.cpp:2766). ProjectVersionStore::prune, run from ProjectAutosave::trim_history after every version, removes every regular file under attachments/ that is not in the document's attachments index (ProjectVersionStore.cpp, final loop). Chat blobs are in neither the index nor live_attachments. Afterwards load_record_bytes gets "" from read_attachment_blob (missing file returns empty) and the next request carries an image block with empty data, permanently, since the record is append-only. Also: a forked managed identity copies only the opened file's attachment folder, so chat blobs are not carried over. Fix: either keep chat blobs somewhere prune never sweeps (own top-level directory in the managed folder, carried on fork and deleted with the chat) or make them part of what prune keeps; and make a missing blob an invariant violation that throws, never an empty picture. Test it through on-disk persistence with the autosave/prune path, not in-memory.

3. CONFIRMED. The record is appended when the transport accepts the post (ProviderAgent.cpp:406, record() right after m_transport->post returns true), not when the provider accepts the request. A 413 or a 400 for a bad or oversized picture then leaves the person's message, workspace block and pictures in the record and the chat can never send again. Fix: append only once the provider has answered 2xx (first stream event or completion), so a rejected request leaves no trace; the "a turn whose request fails" test must distinguish a 503 (message kept, nothing recorded) from a 400/413 (same). Also do the fallible blob write before dispatch, not inside on_recorded after the request is in flight; today an exception there leaves m_busy true with a live request.

4. UNVERIFIED, needs a live check before merge, which Kenneth has to approve (do not make the call yourself): Responses reasoning items are replayed across turns with their ids under store:false and no encrypted_content (ResponsesCodec.cpp:72-76, :155; no include requested). Community reports describe a 404 "Item … not found. Items are not persisted when store is set to false" for exactly this. If true, the failure is permanent per chat. Read OpenAI's current Responses docs on store:false, reasoning items and include=reasoning.encrypted_content and say what the record must keep for replay to be valid; make the codec change if the docs settle it, and say what a live two-turn check should look for.

Smaller findings, fix if cheap and say which you skipped: retrying a failed reply that is not the newest sends a request ending on an assistant item (make_agent_request early return on empty source, AgentHost.cpp:2967; handle_retry does not require the newest message); turn_recorded re-derives "already sent" from attempt>1 && source.empty() when the host knows it exactly via sent(id); a rewritten note is re-sent only when it starts the turn, and each re-send appends a duplicate id to record.messages (ProjectStateDocument.cpp:902); the record is read leniently (value() defaults, unknown part kinds become PDFs) while written strictly, so read with at() and throw on unknown kinds; a reply request with no on_recorded sink is a silent no-op in record() (ProviderAgent.cpp:329), it should throw; each turn start parses the whole record three times and re-reads and base64-encodes every blob on the GUI thread, parse once per turn and avoid the encode/decode round trip if RecordPart holds bytes.

Growth the reviewer judged unnecessary, about 70-90 production lines: start_record_of_earlier_chat repeats the file-report/user/note if-chain and the report label literal from the unsent loop (merge them); record.messages mostly duplicates the items' source fields (store only the ids the migration covered); the keep lambda and load_record_bytes walk the same parts (one for_each_blob); the host builds AgentUnsentMessage and the agent turns it into RecordItems (hand over ready-made items, which also deletes the test-side copy in kept_turn.hpp that already differs from production: it leaves issue_context untagged where production wraps it in <print_issue>); unreachable fallbacks after exhaustive switches. Do these after the four blockers.

Tests the reviewer found missing: the real ProviderAgent over a migrated record; on-disk persistence through autosave and prune; a 4xx after acceptance and what the next turn sends; a host-level retry after the record holds the message (RetryingAgent never calls on_recorded); a stop or failure followed by a new turn under the history-prefix guard; retrying a failed reply that is not the newest.

Same rules as before: no live calls, commit on your branch, agent suite and guard green, update r7-report.md with what changed and the new production diff stat.

The R7 branch is not mergeable. An independent reviewer read it without my expectations, and I confirmed its three worst findings against the code myself. All of it is back with the [R7 session](#local_30027b38-7afd-422d-9cd1-89ded5bdb6f3), which is working on the fixes now.

**The blockers, each a permanent per-chat failure the old code could not produce:**

- **Every chat from before the change throws on its first request.** The migration stores the record with an empty wire format, and the agent loop rejects any non-empty record whose format does not match the provider. The migration test used a fake agent and asserted the empty format, so it recorded exactly the input that crashes the real loop.
- **Autosave deletes the record's pictures.** Chat blobs are written under the project's `attachments/` folder, and the version store's prune, which runs after every autosave, removes every file there that the document's attachment index does not list. After that the chat sends empty image blocks forever, because the record is append-only and a missing blob reads back as empty instead of failing.
- **A rejected request poisons the chat.** The record is appended when the transport accepts the post, not when the provider accepts the request. A 413 or a 400 for an oversized picture then leaves the message in the record, and the chat can never send again.
- **Unverified but likely:** OpenAI reasoning items are replayed across turns by id with `store:false`, which community reports say returns a 404. The session will read the current docs first; a live check comes after, and that is the second decision below.

The reviewer also judged about 70 to 90 of the 361 new production lines to be duplication, and listed six transitions no test covers. Those are in the same message to the session, after the blockers.

**Decision needed, second item.** Finding 4 needs one live two-turn chat on OpenAI gpt-5.4-mini once the rework lands, to confirm whether replaying reasoning items with `store:false` is accepted. It is a few cents, outside the batches you approved under D6, so it needs your yes. Reply "approve the store:false check" or "no".

The decision in the box is the other one: whether the six prompt cases should still expect the print-issues skill. The harness session committed the "no" answer before your instruction to leave it alone reached it, so the commit exists on its branch either way.

Keep a chat's record only of what the provider took, and keep its pictures

A review of the chat record found four problems that would break chats in
use. This fixes three of them and settles the fourth from OpenAI's docs.
Each fix has a test that fails without it.

1. Every chat from before the record threw on its first request. The
   migration stored its record with an empty wire format, and the turn loop
   refused any record whose format differed from the provider's. Now the
   host builds the migrated record in memory and stores it together with
   the first items the provider takes, in their format. The loop's own
   format check is gone. The document's check (append_chat_record) and the
   host's refusal of a model in the other format (record_refusal) remain.
   The migration test now runs the real ProviderAgent on both wire
   formats, not a mock.

2. The version store's prune deleted every picture and PDF the record
   kept. Record blobs lived under attachments/, and ProjectVersionStore::
   prune removes every file there that the document's attachment index
   does not name. They now live in a top-level chats/<conversation>/
   folder, which prune never touches. In managed projects too, the folder
   is deleted with its chat, and importing an archive copies it alongside
   attachments/. A blob missing from disk now throws instead of being sent
   as an empty picture on every later request. Blobs hold the base64 text
   exactly as sent, so neither writing nor reading decodes or re-encodes.

3. The record was appended as soon as the transport accepted the post, not
   when the provider accepted the request. A 400 or 413 caused by a bad
   picture then stayed in the record and broke the chat for good. Now
   items join the record at the provider's first stream event, so a
   refused request (503, 400 or 413) leaves no trace and the person's
   message goes again with the next turn. Picture blobs are written before
   the request that first sends them. A blob that cannot be written stops
   the request before it goes out (the turn fails with the existing
   generic error). Before, a failed write threw from the stream callback
   with the request still in flight.

4. Responses reasoning items replayed under store:false. OpenAI's
   reasoning guide (developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/reasoning) says
   that in stateless mode reasoning output items include encrypted_content
   by default. It calls the include value a legacy option that is not
   required, and says to replay output items untouched. The record already
   keeps them verbatim, ids included, so the codec is unchanged. Only a
   live two-turn check can confirm this.

Smaller fixes:
- Only the chat's last reply can be retried. Retrying an earlier failed
  reply sent a request ending on an assistant item.
- AgentRequest::turn_recorded is set by the host, which knows it, instead
  of being re-derived from attempt and source.
- A rewritten note is sent again whichever turn comes next, not only when
  it starts the turn. The record no longer keeps a list of message ids,
  so a resend no longer adds a duplicate id: ChatRecord::holds() looks at
  the items' sources plus the ids a migration covered.
- The record is read strictly. Fields use at(), and an unknown part or
  item kind throws.
- A reply request with no record sink is a logic error. AgentSetup's key
  check is not a chat, so it passes no-op sinks.
- A turn start reads the record once, not three times.

Trimmed: the host hands the loop ready-made RecordItems for unsent
messages (AgentUnsentMessage is gone, and the test helper now tags print
issues as production does). The migration and the unsent loop share one
message-to-item function. The record-kind name fallback and the codecs'
unreachable switch fallbacks are gone.

What the model sees that is new: when a later request of a turn is
refused or fails, that turn's calls and results are no longer kept. The
next turn sees the person's message and the current workspace, not the
calls the model made.

Not verified: the real prune. ProjectVersionStore needs libslic3r, which
is not built in this worktree, so the managed-project test applies prune's
rule for attachments/ itself. No live request was made.

result.output:
**1. `store: false` / stateless mode and default `encrypted_content`**

The page says stateless mode applies when `store` is `false`: "Stateless mode applies when `store` is `false` or when your organization uses Zero Data Retention (ZDR)." It also says that in stateless mode, "reasoning items in the response's `output` array include an `encrypted_content` property by default." So `encrypted_content` is included by default without setting `include`.

input.message:
Kenneth approved one small live OpenAI run: a two-turn chat on gpt-5.4-mini to prove that the new chat record replays reasoning items under store:false and OpenAI accepts them. Please run it against the merged branch.

Background: `claude/chat-history-cache` is at `87de165901` and now holds your harness branch (all three commits, journey mode included), the trimmed request logger (`f1b3c9a26d`: `--request-log DIR` now writes `NNNN-request.json` byte for byte plus `NNNN-usage.txt`; `log->transport(inner)` takes no provider argument and there is no agent wrapper) and the R7 chat record, which stores each turn's output items as sent and replays them verbatim. The one R7 blocker still resting on docs alone is that reasoning items with `encrypted_content` replay cleanly under `store:false`; OpenAI's guide says they are included by default, and community reports say otherwise. Kenneth kept your `4d663df65c` (the six dropped skill expectations), so nothing to revert.

The job, in your worktree `cache-harness-m4-d222dd` (check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja` first; another session is building the shell harness in `angry-morse-31b9df`, so wait for that ninja to finish before starting yours; `-- -j4`):

2. One chat, two turns, `--plan-journey` on OpenAI with `JUSPRIN_JOURNEY_MODEL=gpt-5.4-mini` and `--request-log DIR`, the shortest journey you have that produces a model reply with reasoning and then a second person turn. Budget: a few cents, so stop the journey after the second turn's reply if the mode allows it, and say if it does not. If the only way is the full M4 journey of one chat, run just one chat and say so before you start.
3. Report: for the second turn's first request, does the body contain a `reasoning` item from turn one with `encrypted_content`? Did the request get a 200 and a reply? Paste the first differing JSON path from `prefix_check.py` for each consecutive pair, the usage lines (input, cached) per request, and the cost at the M4 prices.
4. Commit nothing from the run; the logs stay untracked. If the request fails (404 on an item id or similar), capture the error body verbatim and stop; that is the finding.

Report when done or blocked. No other model calls.
